method.sky: pinneapple_physics.astro: JPL DE421, light time, solar deflection, aberration, IAU 2006/1980 precession-nutation, Saemundsson refraction
method.passes: SGP4 (sgp4 package, Vallado 2006) → TEME → ITRS (GMST82); conical Earth shadow; diffuse-sphere magnitude from the standard magnitude at 1000 km, 90° phase.
method.separation: Vincenty great-circle formula on apparent places of date (topocentric)
method.orbit: Elements from the DE421 heliocentric state (J2000 ecliptic); relativistic Doppler from the topocentric range rate.
method.star: Distance from the BSC5 parallax; Teff from B−V (Ballesteros 2012); BC_V from a black-body V-band integral zero-pointed on the Sun; L and R from Stefan–Boltzmann
method.events: Root finding on apparent geocentric ecliptic longitudes; eclipse geometry with the Danjon shadow enlargement; local solar-eclipse circumstances from topocentric separations.
method.lensing: Schwarzschild null geodesics (RK4 on u″ = 3u² − u) from pinneapple_physics.blackhole; shadow diameter 2√27 GM/(c² D); weak-field deflection 4GM/(c² b)
method.smallbodies: DOP853 test-particle integration in the DE421 field of the Sun, planets and Moon, with the Sun's 1PN relativistic term; no Yarkovsky or asteroid perturbers.
method.surrogateRef: Yoshida 4th-order symplectic N-body (Sun, 8 planets, Moon), dt = 6 h
decay.title: Orbit decay (physics-informed)
decay.training: Training the PINN and the Monte-Carlo envelope on the server (~20 s)…
decay.line: Decay now {rate} m/day · loss over the window {drop} km (5–95 %: {lo}–{hi} km)
decay.sgp4: SGP4 from the loaded TLE (its own drag model): {a} m/day; this model with the same date and solar activity: {b} m/day (ratio {ratio}).
decay.noSgp4: No current ISS TLE loaded, so no SGP4 comparison (the offline check is in the test suite: ratio 0.94 for a 2018 TLE).
decay.how: da/dt = −B ρ(h) √(μ a); ρ: orbit-averaged NRLMSIS 2.0; PINN a(t) = a₀ − s τ softplus(g(τ)) trained on the ODE residual; reference: DOP853 integration; envelope: Monte Carlo over F10.7 (±20 %), Ap (×0.5–2) and B (±15 %). Altitude from the semi-major axis of a near-circular orbit. The ballistic coefficient B is an input (ISS ≈ 0.005 m²/kg: C<sub>D</sub> 2.2, ~950 m² mean cross-section, 420 t); SGP4's B* is not a physical B.
decay.trust: The PINN reproduces the integrator to metres; the forecast itself is limited by the inputs: solar flux and geomagnetic storms weeks ahead are uncertain (shown by the envelope), and the attitude-dependent drag area of a real spacecraft varies.
sw.loading: Loading Kp and training the forecaster (first time ~1 min)…
sw.kpNeeded: Kp needed overhead / on the horizon
sw.sourceLive: Source: NOAA SWPC planetary K index (live).
sw.sourceOffline: Source: offline replay of observed Kp (GFZ), 2000-Nov-25; live NOAA SWPC data unavailable.
sw.how: Quantile MLP (pinball loss) for the change from persistence, on the last 24 h of Kp, the 27-day recurrence and F10.7; split-conformal widening on Sep–Oct; scored on Nov–Dec 2000 against observed Kp (GFZ); aurora boundary 66.5 − 2.04 Kp (geomagnetic latitude, IGRF-13 dipole). At 3 h the network's median lost to persistence on the calibration block, so persistence is used as the median with the calibrated network interval around it.
sw.trust: Trained and scored on one year (2000, solar maximum): it beats persistence at 24 h but misses most storm onsets (they are driven by solar-wind structures it does not see). Treat it as a calibrated range, not a storm warning. Aurora visibility also needs a dark, clear sky.
wx.howLong: Per hour: P(clear sky) = fraction of ensemble members with total cloud < 30 %; cloud cover median and 10–90 %; transparency from cloud and humidity; seeing ranked from the 250 hPa jet-stream wind.
wx.trustLong: The ensemble spread is not yet recalibrated against observations at the site (that needs a forecast/observation history; conditions.calibrate does it). The seeing proxy is a ranking, not arc-seconds.
wx.how: P(clear) = fraction of members with total cloud < 30 %; transparency from cloud and humidity; seeing ranked from the 250 hPa wind.
wx.trust: Probabilities are the raw ensemble spread (uncalibrated); typical NWP cloud forecasts are over-confident beyond 24 h.
sb.none: No approach within 0.2 AU in this window.
sb.apophis: Apophis on {date}: {d} km from the Earth's centre (JPL: {jd} ± {s3} km), {v} km/s (JPL {jv}).
sb.how: Test-particle integration (DOP853, rtol 10⁻¹¹) in the DE421 field of the Sun, the eight planets and the Moon, plus the Sun's 1PN relativistic term, from the JPL SBDB osculating elements.
sb.trust: No Yarkovsky thermal force and no asteroid perturbers: fine for years, not for impact-probability work decades ahead (Apophis's 2068 geometry depends on Yarkovsky).
sb.trainPinn: Train a PINN for the selected body (1 year, ~1 min)
sb.neuralTitle: Learned propagator for many NEOs (one network)
sb.neuralLine: Trained on {ntr} synthetic NEO orbits, tested on {nte} unseen ones. Over a year, deviations from Kepler for near-Earth asteroids are dominated by planetary encounters, which one network trained on ~1,000 orbits does not generalise; the gate rejects it and the app uses the integrator (and per-body PINNs) instead.
sb.neuralHow: An MLP maps the osculating elements at the epoch and the time to the deviation from the Kepler orbit (radial / along-track / normal), trained on the full integrator; early stopping on held-out bodies.
sb.neuralTrust: Not used for any result in the app: the gate rejects it. Kept to show what the trust checks catch.
sb.pinnTraining: Training the PINN for {body} on the server…
sb.pinnLine: max error (held-out times) {km} km = {arcsec}″ from the Sun; Kepler alone {kep} km; trained in {s} s.
sb.pinnHow: r(t) = r<sub>Kepler</sub>(t) + τ² g<sub>θ</sub>(τ): the network learns the planetary perturbation only, from the residual of the full N-body equation of motion (planets from DE421) and 8 anchor states; split-conformal band on held-out integrator states.
sb.pinnTrust: Valid for this body over this year; it is a compact, differentiable surrogate of one trajectory, not a general propagator.

ml.line: {n} stars with a trigonometric parallax ≥ 5 mas ({nl} with an MK luminosity class). Luminosity class: {acc} % (baseline {base} %); recall {rec}. Spectral class from B−V: {sacc} % (baseline {sbase} %).
ml.how: Gaussian mixture (EM) on (B−V, M_V); k-nearest neighbours (k = 15, standardised features), 5-fold cross-validation against the BSC5 MK spectral types. The clusters are found without labels and only named afterwards by their majority MK class.
ml.trust: Subgiants and bright giants are hard (few examples, they sit between the branches): their recall is low, as the table says. Colours are not dereddened; BSC5 parallaxes are pre-Hipparcos.

bh.caption: A Schwarzschild black hole with a thin accretion disc (exact null geodesics; inner edge at the ISCO, 6 GM/c²; Keplerian gas; Doppler beaming and gravitational redshift, g⁴ intensity) in front of the real stars and Milky Way around RA {ra}°, Dec {dec}°. The disc's far side appears above and below the shadow because its light is bent around the hole.
bh.zooNote: The black-hole accretion forecaster is not in the model zoo yet (or has not passed its gate); its forecast and skill horizon will appear here when it does.
eng.title: Physics-informed orbit surrogate
eng.intro: A PINN learns a planet's heliocentric orbit for the next year: r(t) = rKepler(t) + τ² gθ(τ), trained on the residual of the full N-body equation of motion plus 8 anchor states, then judged against the classical integrator with split-conformal bands and physics checks.

eng.reference: Reference: {method}; its total energy drift {e}, angular momentum {l}. Energy / angular-momentum checks compare the PINN's error with the size of the perturbation-induced variation.
eng.intNote: Sun, 8 planets and the Moon from DE421 at J2000, 6-hour steps for two years. Symplectic schemes keep the energy error bounded; RK4 drifts. Against DE421 the Newtonian point-mass model misses relativity and asteroids (Mars: ~{km} km after 2 yr).
